To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the protein of interest is a soluble protein that is retained in the ER; (2) this protein is not retained in the ER of cells that lack the protein(s) of interest; (3) this protein does not interact with the protein of interest; and (4) this protein does interact with the protein(s) that are responsible for retaining the protein of interest in the ER.
the export of soluble cargo proteins from the ER to the Golgi apparatus is not a passive process.
the ER retention of a soluble protein is due to the interaction with a resident protein, and this interaction is regulated by the folding status of the soluble protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of protein retention in the endoplasmatic reticulum (er).
the role of the endoplasmatic reticulum (er) in the regulation of cell death.
the mechanisms that regulate the retention of soluble proteins in the ER.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ER export of soluble proteins is a two-step process.
the retention of soluble proteins in the ER is a dynamic process and is dependent upon both retrieval and retention mechanisms.
the export of soluble ER proteins from the ER is mediated by a retrieval pathway, and that this retrieval pathway can be modulated by the presence of a retention signal in the ER.

we have demonstrated that soluble proteins are retained in the endoplasm...
the export of soluble ER proteins occurs by two mechanisms: retrieval of proteins that have already entered the secretory pathway and retention of proteins that are not exported from the ER.
the ER is a dynamic organelle that is able to regulate the export of proteins to the Golgi and the cell surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the retention of proteins in the ER is not a passive phenomenon, it is an active process.
the protein is not retained in the endoplasmatic reticulum, it is retrieved from the endoplamic reticulum and degraded by the proteasome.
the ER has a mechanism for retaining soluble proteins that is different from that used for membrane proteins.
